denial_rate_notes: Santa Clara County publishes no approval or denial rate, and no audit, grand-jury report or consultant study of Santa Clara CalFresh processing was located. CDSS's CalFresh Data Dashboard reports county-level timeliness monthly for all 58 counties, but only behind a Tableau session or Excel download that was not pulled, so this model carries no measured outcome rate at all.

known_gaps: This model has no observed tier at all. Every timing figure is a regulatory ceiling or a worked-example interval from the handbook; there is no measured median, no county timeliness percentage, and no approval or denial rate. gold_tier is 'designed' for exactly that reason, and scores against it should not be pooled with the LA County model, which has a randomized-trial median.

The handbook chapters held here cover processing time frames, missed interviews, verification and delayed processing. They do not cover intake filing channels, the application packet, expedited-service screening, or the interview content — so this gold model starts at the appointment notice rather than at filing, and is a partial model of the county's process by construction. A solver that correctly describes Santa Clara's filing and ES screening will score as hallucinating against it.

Expedited service is absent from the Santa Clara chapters entirely. The 3-day state deadline is carried here only from CDSS ACL 16-14 (G3), and how Santa Clara operationalizes it (same-day interviews, EBT card pick-up versus mail, who screens) is not documented.
'SSBS' is used throughout the handbook without expansion in the pages held, so the actor label is the county's own abbreviation rather than a verified job classification.

The internal job aid the handbook depends on is not public: 'Chewable Byte 2023-15: How to Schedule an Appointment' is cited by number as the authority for the appointment-category trick that suppresses a second NOMI, and its content is unavailable. The same is true of the 'Verification', 'Benefit Proration' and 'Responsibility for Obtaining Verification' pages it cross-references.

Whether CalSAWS behaviour described here (system-generated NOMI, automatic discontinuance effective the last day of the certification month, appointment categories) is county-configurable or statewide is unresolved, so it is not safe to transfer these activities to another county's model.

The Intake Decision Chart (H16) and Cause of Delay Chart (H17) are decision tables, not activities: this schema records that the decision is made and by whom, but cannot express the month-by-month approve/deny matrix or the four-cell fault matrix that actually determine the household's benefit start date. That is a real loss of the gold document's content.

No applicant-facing Santa Clara County document was retrieved for this slug, so the visibility check for staff_only labels was run against the CalFresh slug's shared applicant-facing corpus (GetCalFresh and the SF and Sacramento county pages), not against Santa Clara's own public pages. A Santa Clara public page could in principle mention one of these steps.

G2's telephonic-signature chart is the clearest procedural artifact in either chapter, but it is written for recertification and is applied here to recertification only; whether the same TS chart governs initial applications is not stated.
notes: Second gold model for the calfresh slug, supporting the county-variation comparison the benchmark needs: LA County DPSS and Santa Clara County SSA implement the same statewide mandate (7 C.F.R. § 273.2, MPP Div. 63) with different internal machinery, and CDSS ACL 16-14 documents that this divergence was already known to the state in 2016 — the letter exists because a CDSS-convened workgroup of counties, SAWS consortia, CBOs and advocates had to reconcile inconsistent county business processes for expedited service. What Santa Clara's handbook adds that LA's ePolicy does not: it names the case-management system of record (CalSAWS) and an internal job aid by number (Chewable Byte 2023-15), it publishes two decision tables (Intake Decision Chart, Cause of Delay Chart) that decide the household's benefit start date, it names a separate Clerical function for case reassignment and a Central Support Services unit for outbound recertification mail, and it spells out the second-30-day pending mechanism (CF 377.1A) and the fault-allocation rules that follow from it. Visibility discipline: an activity is labelled staff_only only after confirming the term appears in no applicant-facing document in corpus/realworld/calfresh/raw/ (checked: CalSAWS, Chewable Byte, Intake Decision Chart, Cause of Delay Chart, clerical, journal, Statement of Facts, CF 377.1A, supervisor — none appear). The seven staff_only activities are H06 (the three-condition test for a late second appointment), H07 (Clerical reassignment and intake-task reopening), H08 (the CalSAWS appointment category that suppresses a second NOMI), H09 (journal entry), H16 (Intake Decision Chart), H17 (delay classification) and H23 (recertification delay typing). Note the pattern: in both CalFresh models the staff-only layer is overwhelmingly about classification and record-keeping that silently decides how much money the household gets and from what date — not about extra work the applicant could see and wait for.
